elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 7.2(e): "The Issuer, as the customer under this Agreement, may, for convenience and without cause, remove the Servicer and terminate the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice..." This is an unconditional Customer election with no cause requirement, i.e. a convenience right. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" reads false, but that is a phrasing artefact: the clause terminates the Vendor's engagement rather than reciting "terminate this Agreement". Substantively the Customer's exit from the Servicer relationship is granted; there are no Order Forms in this structure, and Agreement-level termination under Section 8.3 is the securitization wind-down trigger, not the customer/vendor engagement.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2(e) requires "thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer" — exactly the 30-day ceiling; Section 7.3 fixes effectiveness at the date stated in the notice of termination, so no longer wind-down is imposed on the Customer's exercise.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2(e): "the Servicer will refund, pro rata, any Servicing Fees paid in advance for any period after the effective date of the termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely post-termination-period) and is owed by the Vendor. That Servicing Fees are ordinarily paid in arrears makes the limb protective, not defective.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.1 No Resignation: "The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement" — resignation is permitted only on legal inability, which is not a convenience right, and no other Vendor at-will exit appears. Left untouched, correctly.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2(e) sets thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback window. This is a Customer-favourable overshoot and is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty, make-whole or instalment mechanic attaches to the new Section 7.2(e) removal (the Section 8.1/8.2 Make-Whole Payment attaches to Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption, not to this right), so nothing exceeds a three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori and vacuously: Section 7.1 bars Servicer resignation altogether except on legal inability, so there is no Vendor convenience right that could be exercised at any point, let alone mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — the Vendor has no convenience termination right under Section 7.1, so no notice floor is required. Correctly not redlined, since importing the fallback would create a Vendor exit that does not currently exist.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted Section 7.2(e) supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day notice, and the pro rata prepaid-fee refund, and retained Section 7.1 already denies the Servicer any convenience exit.

The deterministic flag "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a false negative on substance. The insertion grants the Issuer an unconditional, cause-free election to end the Servicer's engagement; that is a convenience right under the rule's own boundary. If the drafter wants belt-and-braces, the phrase "terminate the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement" could be expanded to "...and, at the Issuer's election, this Agreement as it relates to the Servicer", but no repair is required for completeness.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, no favourable retained language (Section 7.1 No Resignation, Section 7.2(c) Cellco reassumption, Section 7.3, Section 7.4(a)(i), Section 8.3) is touched, no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or damages language is added, and no duplicate convenience mechanic is created. The descriptor "as the customer under this Agreement" is a short identifying gloss rather than an added operative requirement.

Intent preserved: placing the right in Section 7.2 makes the exercise a "removal ... pursuant to this Section 7.2", so the Cellco reassumption sentence, the Section 7.3 continue-to-perform date-stated-in-notice mechanic, and the party-agnostic Section 7.4(a)(i) Successor Servicer engagement all engage without conforming edits; Section 8.3's Agreement-level triggers and the Section 8.1/8.2 Certificateholder options are untouched, leaving no dangling cross-reference, undefined term, or contradictory retained sentence.

Deviation finding is correct: before the edit the only Customer-side exit was cause-based removal on a continuing Servicer Termination Event under Section 7.2(c), in a term running until the last Receivable is paid (Section 8.3) — walk-away territory under this rule.
Fallback is deliberately not targeted and is not met (30 days is shorter than the 60–90 day band); that is a Customer-favourable overshoot within the preferred position and not a defect.
